cues.en: Do you bring this trick out at parties? Oh, no. It's a terrible party trick. Here we go.
cues.zh: 你会在派对上露这手吗？哦不，这当派对把戏太烂了。我们开始吧。

cues.en: This is Grant Gusman. He watched an old video of mine about how we think that there are two systems of thought. System two is the conscious,
cues.zh: 这位是 Grant Gusman。他看过我之前的一期视频，讲的是人类思考的双系统理论。系统二是意识层面的、

cues.en: slow, effortful system.
cues.zh: 缓慢且费力的系统。

cues.en: And system one is subconscious,
cues.zh: 而系统一是潜意识的、

cues.en: fast and automatic.
cues.zh: 快速且自动化的。

cues.en: To
cues.zh: 为了

cues.en: explore how these systems work in his own head, Grant decided to memorize a 100 digits of pi. Three eight four four six zero... Then he just kept going. He has now memorized 23,000
cues.zh: 探究这两个系统在自己大脑中是如何运作的，Grant 决定背诵圆周率的前 100 位。3-8-4-4-6-0……然后他就停不下来了。如今他已经背下了 23,000

cues.en: digits of pi in preparation to challenge the North American record. Eight nine five four nine three zero three eight one nine six. That's 200.
That's amazing.
cues.zh: 太不可思议了。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: have wanted to make a video about experts for a long time.
cues.zh: 很久以来就想做一期关于“专家”的视频了。

cues.en: This is Magnus Carlsen, the five time world chess champion. He's being shown chess boards and asked to identify the game in which they occurred. This
cues.zh: 这位是 Magnus Carlsen，五届国际象棋世界冠军。节目组给他看一些残局盘面，让他辨认出自哪场对局。这盘

cues.en: looks an awful lot like
cues.zh: 看起来非常像

cues.en: Talbotwynik.
cues.zh: Talbotwynik。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: This is the twenty fourth game from Seville, obviously.
cues.zh: 这显然是塞维利亚世锦赛的第 24 局。

cues.en: Now, I'm going to play through an opening and
cues.zh: 现在，我要摆一个开局走法，

cues.en: stop me when you recognize the game and if you can tell me who was playing black in this one. Okay. Sure. Okay.
cues.zh: 你认出对局就喊停，顺便告诉我执黑的是谁。好的，没问题，好。

cues.en: I'm sure you've seen this opening before. Okay. It's gonna be Arnold.
cues.zh: 我相信你肯定见过这个开局。好的，执黑的是 Arnold。

cues.en: Against...
cues.zh: 对阵……

cues.en: Sabata.
cues.zh: Sabata。

cues.en: How can he do this? It seems like superhuman ability.
cues.zh: 他是怎么做到的？这简直像超能力一样。

cues.en: Well, decades ago, scientists wanted to know what makes experts like chess masters special.
cues.zh: 其实几十年前，科学家就想弄明白，像国际象棋特级大师这样的专家究竟特殊在哪里。

cues.en: Do they have incredibly high IQs?
cues.zh: 是因为他们智商极高吗？

cues.en: Much better spatial reasoning than average? Bigger short term memory spans.
cues.zh: 空间推理能力远超常人？短时记忆容量更大？

cues.en: Well, it turns out that as a group, chess masters are not exceptional on any of these measures.
cues.zh: 然而事实证明，作为一个群体，国际象棋大师在这些指标上并不出众。

cues.en: But one experiment showed how their performance was vastly superior to amateurs.
cues.zh: 但有一项实验揭示了他们远胜于业余选手的地方。

cues.en: William Chase and Herbert Simon recruited three chess players, a master, an a player who's an advanced amateur,
cues.zh: William Chase 和 Herbert Simon 招募了三位棋手：一位大师、一位高级业余选手（A 级棋手），

cues.en: and a beginner.
cues.zh: 以及一位初学者。

cues.en: A chessboard was set up with around 25 pieces positioned as they might be during a game and each player was allowed to look at the board for five seconds.
cues.zh: 棋盘上摆了大约 25 枚棋子，呈现真实对局中可能出现的局面，每位棋手可以看棋盘 5 秒钟。

cues.en: Then they were asked to replicate the setup from memory on a second board in front of them. The players could take as many five second peaks as they needed to get their board to match.
cues.zh: 然后要求他们凭记忆在面前的第二个棋盘上复原棋局。棋手想看几次都行，每次 5 秒，直到完全对上为止。

cues.en: From just the first look, the master could recall the positions of 16 pieces.
cues.zh: 仅仅看第一眼，大师就能记起 16 枚棋子的位置。

cues.en: The a player could recall eight and the beginner only four.
cues.zh: A 级棋手能记起 8 枚，而初学者只能记起 4 枚。

cues.en: The master only needed half the number of peaks as the a player to get their board perfect.
cues.zh: 大师要达到完全复原所需的看盘次数，只有 A 级棋手的一半。

cues.en: But then the researchers arranged the board with pieces in random positions that would never arise in a real game.
cues.zh: 但随后，研究人员把棋子随机散落在棋盘上，摆出实战中绝不可能出现的局面。

cues.en: And now, the chess master performed no better than the beginner.
cues.zh: 结果，特级大师的表现并不比初学者强。

cues.en: After the first look, all players regardless of rank could remember the location of only three pieces.
cues.zh: 第一眼过后，无论水平高低，所有棋手都只能记住三个棋子的位置。

cues.en: The data are clear. Chess experts don't have better memory in general, but they have better memory specifically for chess positions that could occur in a real game. The implication is what makes chess masters special is that they have seen lots and lots of chess games.
cues.zh: 数据很清楚。国际象棋专家并不是一般记忆力更好，而是对真实对局中可能出现的棋局有更好的记忆。这说明，国际象棋大师的特殊之处在于他们看过大量国际象棋对局。

cues.en: And over that time, their brains have learned patterns.
cues.zh: 而在这段时间里，他们的大脑学会了模式。

cues.en: So rather than seeing individual pieces at individual positions,
cues.zh: 所以，他们看到的不是各个位置上的单个棋子，

cues.en: they see a smaller number of recognizable
cues.zh: 而是看到数量更少的、可识别的

cues.en: configurations.
cues.zh: 配置。

cues.en: This is called chunking.
cues.zh: 这叫作组块化。

cues.en: What we have stored in long term memory allows us to recognize complex stimuli
cues.zh: 我们存储在长期记忆中的内容，让我们能把复杂刺激识别为

cues.en: as just one thing. For example, you recognize this as pie rather than a string of six unrelated numbers or meaningless squiggles for that matter.
cues.zh: 一个整体。例如，你把这个识别为 π，而不是一串六个互不相关的数字，或者一堆无意义的涂鸦。

cues.en: There's a wonderful sequence I like a lot which is three zero one seven three
cues.zh: 有一个我特别喜欢的美妙序列：三零一七三

cues.en: which to me means Stephen Curry number 30
cues.zh: 对我来说，它意味着 Stephen Curry 的 30 号

cues.en: won 73 games which is the record back in 2016. So 30173.
cues.zh: 赢下 73 场比赛，这是 2016 年的纪录。所以就是 30173。

cues.en: At its core, expertise
cues.zh: 从根本上说，专业技能

cues.en: is about recognition.
cues.zh: 就是识别。

cues.en: Magnus Carlsen recognizes chest positions the same way we recognize faces
cues.zh: Magnus Carlsen 识别棋盘局面的方式，就像我们识别人脸一样

cues.en: and recognition leads directly to intuition.
cues.zh: 而识别会直接通向直觉。

cues.en: If you see an angry face, you have a pretty good idea of what's gonna come next.
cues.zh: 如果你看到一张愤怒的脸，你大概能猜到接下来会发生什么。

cues.en: Chess masters recognize board positions and instinctively know the best move. Most of the time,
cues.zh: 国际象棋大师能识别棋盘局面，并本能地知道最佳着法。大多数时候，

cues.en: I know what to do.
cues.zh: 我知道该怎么做。

cues.en: I don't have to
cues.zh: 我不必

cues.en: figure it out.
cues.zh: 去把它算出来。

cues.en: To develop the long term memory of an expert takes a long time. Ten thousand hours is the rule of thumb popularized by Malcolm Gladwell,
cues.zh: 培养专家的长期记忆需要很长时间。一万小时是 Malcolm Gladwell 推广的经验法则，

cues.en: but ten thousand hours of practice by itself is not sufficient.
cues.zh: 但仅仅一万小时的练习还不够。

cues.en: There are four additional criteria that must be met.
cues.zh: 还必须满足四个额外条件。

cues.en: And in areas where these criteria aren't met, it's impossible to become an expert.
cues.zh: 而在不满足这些条件的领域，就不可能成为专家。

cues.en: So the first one is many repeated attempts with feedback.
cues.zh: 第一个是大量重复尝试，并获得反馈。

cues.en: Tennis players hit hundreds of forehands in practice.
cues.zh: 网球运动员在练习中会打数百次正手。

cues.en: Chess players play thousands of games before their grandmasters,
cues.zh: 国际象棋棋手在成为特级大师之前会下数千盘棋，

cues.en: and physicists solve thousands of physics problems.
cues.zh: 物理学家会解数千道物理题。

cues.en: Each one gets feedback. The tennis player sees whether each shot clears the net and is in or out. The chess player either wins or loses the game, and the physicist gets the problem right or wrong.
cues.zh: 每个人都会得到反馈。网球运动员看到每次击球是否过网、是界内还是界外。国际象棋棋手要么赢要么输，物理学家则知道题目做对还是做错。

cues.en: But some professionals don't get repeated experience with the same sorts of problems.
cues.zh: 但有些专业人士不会反复遇到同类问题。

cues.en: Political scientist Philip Tetlock picked 284
cues.zh: 政治学家 Philip Tetlock 挑选了 284

cues.en: people who make their living commenting or offering advice on political and economic trends. This included journalists,
cues.zh: 名以评论或提供政治与经济趋势建议为生的人。其中包括记者、

cues.en: foreign policy specialists, economists, and intelligence analysts.
cues.zh: 外交政策专家、经济学家和情报分析师。

cues.en: Over two decades, he peppered them with questions like, would George Bush be reelected?
cues.zh: 在二十年里，他不断向他们抛出问题，比如：George Bush 会连任吗？

cues.en: Would apartheid in South Africa end peacefully?
cues.zh: 南非的种族隔离会和平结束吗？

cues.en: Would Quebec secede from Canada?
cues.zh: 魁北克会从加拿大独立吗？

cues.en: And would the .com bubble burst?
cues.zh: .com 泡沫会破裂吗？

cues.en: In each case, the pundits rated the probability of several possible outcomes. And by the end of the study, Tetlock had quantified 82,361
cues.zh: 每一种情况中，权威评论员都评估了几种可能结果的概率。到研究结束时，Tetlock 已经量化了 82,361

cues.en: predictions.
cues.zh: 条预测。

cues.en: So how did they do?
cues.zh: 那他们表现如何？

cues.en: Pretty terribly.
cues.zh: 相当糟糕。

cues.en: These experts, most of whom had postgraduate degrees performed worse than if they had just assigned equal probabilities to all the outcomes.
cues.zh: 这些专家大多拥有研究生学位，但他们的表现还不如直接给所有结果分配相同概率。

cues.en: In other words, people who spend their time and earn their living studying a particular topic produced poorer predictions than random chance.
cues.zh: 换句话说，花时间并以研究某个特定主题为生的人，做出的预测还不如随机猜测。

cues.en: Even in the areas they knew best, experts were not significantly better than non specialists.
cues.zh: 即使在他们最熟悉的领域，专家也并没有显著优于非专家。

cues.en: The problem is most of the events they have to predict are one offs. They haven't had the experience of going through these events or very similar ones many times before.
cues.zh: 问题在于，他们必须预测的大多数事件都是一次性的。他们之前没有多次经历过这些事件或非常相似的事件。

cues.en: Even presidential elections only happen infrequently and each one in a slightly different environment.
cues.zh: 就连总统选举也不常发生，而且每次所处的环境都略有不同。

cues.en: So we should be wary of experts who don't have repeated experience with feedback.
cues.zh: 所以，我们应该警惕那些没有反复获得反馈经验的专家。

cues.en: The next requirement is a valid environment.
cues.zh: 下一个要求是有效环境。

cues.en: One that contains regularities
cues.zh: 一个包含规律的环境，

cues.en: that make it at least somewhat predictable.
cues.zh: 使其至少在一定程度上可预测。

cues.en: A gambler betting at the roulette wheel for example may have thousands of repeated experiences with the same event. And for each one they get clear feedback in the form of whether they win or lose.
cues.zh: 例如，在轮盘赌上下注的赌徒可能对同一事件有成千上万次重复经历。而且每一次他们都会得到明确的反馈：赢还是输。

cues.en: But you would rightfully not consider them an expert because the environment is low validity.
cues.zh: 但你有理由不把他们视为专家，因为这个环境的有效性很低。

cues.en: A roulette wheel is essentially random, so there are no regularities to be learned.
cues.zh: 轮盘赌本质上是随机的，所以没有什么规律可学。

cues.en: legendary investor Warren Buffett offered to bet a million dollars that he could pick an investment that would outperform Wall Street's best hedge funds over a ten year period.
cues.zh: 传奇投资者 Warren Buffett 提出用一百万美元打赌：他能挑选一项投资，在十年内跑赢华尔街最好的对冲基金。

cues.en: Hedge funds are pools of money that are actively managed by some of the brightest and most experienced traders on Wall Street. They use advanced techniques like short selling, leverage, and derivatives in an attempt to provide outsized returns.
cues.zh: 对冲基金是由华尔街一些最聪明、最有经验的交易员主动管理的资金池。他们使用卖空、杠杆和衍生品等高级技巧，试图获得超额回报。

cues.en: And consequently, they charge significant fees.
cues.zh: 因此，他们收取高额费用。

cues.en: One person took Buffett up on the bet, Ted Seides of Protege Partners.
cues.zh: 有一个人接受了巴菲特的赌约，就是 Protege Partners 的 Ted Seides。

cues.en: For his investment, he selected five hedge funds. Well, actually five funds of hedge funds. So in total, a collection of over 200
cues.zh: 在投资选择上，他选了五只对冲基金。嗯，其实是五只对冲基金的基金。所以总共是一个包含 200 多只

cues.en: individual funds.
cues.zh: 单独基金的集合。

cues.en: Warren Buffett took a very different approach. He picked the most basic boring investment imaginable,
cues.zh: Warren Buffett 采用了非常不同的方法。他选了能想到的最基础、最无聊的投资，

cues.en: a passive index fund that just tracks the weighted value the 500 biggest public companies in America, the S and P five hundred.
cues.zh: 一只被动指数基金，只追踪美国 500 家最大上市公司的加权市值，也就是 S&P 500。

cues.en: They started the bet on 01/01/2008
cues.zh: 他们在 2008 年 1 月 1 日开始打赌，

cues.en: and immediately things did not look good for Buffett.
cues.zh: 而一开始情况对巴菲特就不妙。

cues.en: It was the start of the global financial crisis and the market tanked.
cues.zh: 那是在全球金融危机爆发之初，市场暴跌。

cues.en: But the hedge funds could change their holdings and even profit from market falls.
cues.zh: 但对冲基金可以调整持仓，甚至从市场下跌中获利。

cues.en: So they lost some value but not as much as the market average.
cues.zh: 所以它们损失了一些价值，但没有市场平均水平那么多。

cues.en: The hedge funds stayed ahead for the next three years, but by 2011, the S and P 500 had pulled even.
cues.zh: 对冲基金在接下来三年里保持领先，但到2011年，S&P 500已经追平。

cues.en: And from then on, it wasn't even close. The market average surged leaving the hedge funds in the dust. After ten years, Buffett's index fund gained a 125.8%
cues.zh: 从那以后，差距就彻底拉开了。市场平均大幅飙升，把对冲基金远远甩在后面。十年后，Buffett的指数基金收益为125.8%

cues.en: to the hedge funds 36%.
cues.zh: 而对冲基金是36%。

cues.en: Now the market performance was not unusual over this time. At eight and a half percent annual growth, it nearly matches the stock market's long run average. So why did so many investment professionals with years of industry experience, research at their fingertips, and big financial incentives to perform fail to beat the market?
cues.zh: 这段时间的市场表现并不罕见。年增长8.5%，几乎与股市长期平均水平相当。那么，为什么这么多拥有多年行业经验、手边就有研究资料、又有巨大财务激励的投资专业人士，却没能跑赢市场？

cues.en: Well, because stocks are a low validity environment.
cues.zh: 因为股票是一个低效度环境。

cues.en: Over the short term, stock price movements are almost entirely random. So the feedback, although clear and immediate, doesn't actually reflect anything about the quality of the decision making.
cues.zh: 短期来看，股价波动几乎完全是随机的。所以反馈虽然清晰且即时，却并不真正反映决策质量。

cues.en: It's closer to a roulette wheel than to chess.
cues.zh: 它更像轮盘赌，而不是国际象棋。

cues.en: Over a ten year period, around 80% of all actively managed investment funds fail to beat the market average. And if you look at longer time periods, underperformance rises to 90%.
cues.zh: 在十年期内，约80%的主动管理投资基金未能跑赢市场平均水平。而看更长时间段，跑输比例会升到90%。

cues.en: And before you say, well, that means 10% of managers have actual skill,
cues.zh: 在你认为“那说明10%的基金经理真有本事”之前，

cues.en: consider that just through random chance, some people would beat the market anyway. Portfolios picked by cats or throwing darts have been shown to do just that. And in addition to luck, there are nefarious practices from insider trading to pump and dump schemes.
cues.zh: 想想看，仅凭随机概率，也会有人碰巧跑赢市场。已有研究表明，由猫选出的投资组合或靠掷飞镖选出的组合也能做到这一点。而且除了运气，还有从内幕交易到拉高出货的各种不正当操作。

cues.en: Now I don't mean to say there are no expert investors. I mean, Warren Buffett himself is a clear example.
cues.zh: 我不是说没有专业投资者。Warren Buffett本人就是明显例子。

cues.en: But the vast majority of stock pickers and active investment managers do not demonstrate expert performance because of the low validity of their environment.
cues.zh: 但绝大多数选股者和主动投资经理并未展现出专家级表现，因为他们所处环境的效度很低。

cues.en: Brief side note, if we know that stock picking will usually yield worse results over the long term and that what active managers charge in fees is rarely compensated for in improved performance,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，如果我们知道选股长期通常收益更差，而且主动管理经理收取的费用很少能由业绩提升来弥补，

cues.en: then why is so much money invested in individual stocks, mutual funds, and hedge funds?
cues.zh: 那为什么还有这么多钱投在个股、共同基金和对冲基金里？

cues.en: Well, let me answer that with a story. There was an experiment carried out with rats and humans where there's a red button and a green button that can each light up.
cues.zh: 让我用一个故事来回答。有一项用老鼠和人做的实验，实验里有一个红色按钮和一个绿色按钮，每个都能亮起来。

cues.en: 80% of the time, the green button lights up and 20% of the time, the red button lights up, but randomly.
cues.zh: 80%的情况下绿灯亮，20%的情况下红灯亮，但亮起是随机的。

cues.en: So you can never be sure which button will light. And the task for the subject, either rat or human, is to guess beforehand which button will light up by pressing it. For the rat, if they guess right, they get a bit of food, and if they guess wrong, a mild electric shock.
cues.zh: 所以你永远无法确定哪个按钮会亮。实验对象——无论是老鼠还是人——的任务，是提前按下按钮来猜哪个会亮。对老鼠来说，猜对了会得到一点食物，猜错了会受到轻微电击。

cues.en: The rat quickly learns to press only the green button and accept the 80% win percentage.
cues.zh: 老鼠很快学会只按绿色按钮，并接受 80% 的胜率。

cues.en: Humans, on the other hand, usually press the green button, but once in a while, they try to predict when the red light will go on. And as a result, they guess right only 68%
cues.zh: 另一方面，人类通常会按绿色按钮，但偶尔会试图预测红灯何时亮起。结果他们只在 68%

cues.en: of the time.
cues.zh: 的情况下猜对。

cues.en: We have a hard time accepting average results and we see patterns everywhere including
cues.zh: 我们很难接受平均结果，而且我们到处都能看到规律，包括

cues.en: in randomness. So we try to beat the average by predicting the pattern.
cues.zh: 在随机性中。所以我们试图通过预测规律来战胜平均。

cues.en: But when there is no pattern,
cues.zh: 但如果没有规律，

cues.en: this is a terrible strategy.
cues.zh: 这就是个糟糕的策略。

cues.en: Even when there are patterns, you need timely feedback in order to learn them. And YouTube knows this, which is why within the first hour after posting a video, they tell you how its performance compares to your last 10 videos. There's even confetti fireworks when the video is number one. I know it seems like a silly thing, but you have no idea how powerful a reward this is and how much YouTuber effort is spent chasing this supercharged
cues.zh: 即便存在规律，你也需要及时反馈才能学会它们。YouTube 深知这一点，所以视频发布后的第一个小时内，它会告诉你这条视频的表现与你最近 10 条视频相比如何。视频排名第一时，甚至还有彩纸烟花。我知道这听起来很傻，但你不知道这种奖励有多强大，也不知道 YouTuber 为了追逐这种超强

cues.en: dopamine hit.
cues.zh: 多巴胺快感付出了多少努力。

cues.en: To understand the difference between immediate and delayed feedback, psychologist Daniel Kahneman contrasts the experiences of anesthesiologists
cues.zh: 为了理解即时反馈和延迟反馈的区别，心理学家 Daniel Kahneman 对比了麻醉医生

cues.en: and radiologists.
cues.zh: 和放射科医生的经历。

cues.en: Anesthesiologists
cues.zh: 麻醉医生

cues.en: work alongside the patient and get feedback straight away. Is the patient unconscious with stable vital signs? With this immediate feedback, it's easier for them to learn the regularities of their environment.
cues.zh: 会和病人待在一起，并立刻得到反馈。病人是否昏迷且生命体征稳定？有了这种即时反馈，他们更容易学会所处环境中的规律。

cues.en: Radiologists,
cues.zh: 放射科医生

cues.en: on the other hand, don't get rapid feedback on their diagnoses if they get it at all. This makes it much harder for them to improve.
cues.zh: 则不同，他们对自己的诊断得不到快速反馈，甚至根本得不到反馈。这让他们更难进步。

cues.en: Radiologists
cues.zh: 放射科医生

cues.en: typically correctly diagnose breast cancer from x rays just seventy percent of the time.
cues.zh: 通常仅凭 X 光片正确诊断乳腺癌的比例只有 70%。

cues.en: Delayed feedback also seems to be a problem for college admissions officers and recruitment specialists.
cues.zh: 延迟反馈似乎也是大学招生官和招聘专员面临的问题。

cues.en: After admitting someone to college or hiring someone at a big company, you may never or only much later find out how they did. This makes it harder to recognize the patterns in ideal candidates.
cues.zh: 在录取某人或在大公司录用某人之后，你可能永远不知道，或者很久以后才知道他们表现如何。这让你更难识别理想候选人的模式。

cues.en: In one study, Richard Melton tried to predict the grades of freshmen at the end of their first year of college. A set of 14 counselors interviewed each student for forty five minutes to an hour. They also had access to high school grades, several aptitude tests, and a four page personal statement.
cues.zh: 在一项研究中，Richard Melton 试图预测大一学生第一学年结束时的成绩。14 位辅导员每人面试学生 45 分钟到 1 小时。他们还能看到高中成绩、几项能力测试以及一份四页的个人陈述。

cues.en: For comparison, Melton created an algorithm that used as input only a fraction of the information, just high school grades and one aptitude test. Nevertheless,
cues.zh: 作为对比，Melton 创建了一个算法，只把一小部分信息作为输入，即高中成绩和一项能力测试。尽管如此，

cues.en: the formula was more accurate than 11 of the 14 counselors.
cues.zh: 这个公式比 14 位辅导员中的 11 位都更准确。

cues.en: Melton's study was reported alongside over a dozen similar results across a variety of other domains from predicting who would violate parole to who'd succeed in pilot training. If you've ever been denied admission to an educational institution or turned down for a job, it feels like an expert has considered your potential and decided that you don't have what it takes to succeed. You know, I was rejected twice from film school and twice from a drama program. So it's comforting to know that the gatekeepers at these institutions aren't great predictors of future success.
cues.zh: Melton 的研究与十多项类似结果一同被报道，这些结果横跨多种领域，从预测谁会违反假释，到谁能在飞行员训练中成功。如果你曾被某个教育机构拒绝录取，或求职被拒，那感觉就像有位专家评估了你的潜力，并认定你不具备成功的条件。你知道，我曾两次被电影学院拒绝，也两次被戏剧项目拒绝。所以，知道这些机构的守门人并不擅长预测未来成功，还挺让人欣慰的。

cues.en: So if you're in a valid environment and you get repeated experience with the same events with clear timely feedback for each attempt, will you definitely become an expert in ten thousand hours or so? The answer unfortunately is no because most of us want to be comfortable.
cues.zh: 那么，如果你身处一个有效环境中，对相同事件反复历练，且每次尝试都能获得清晰及时的反馈，你花上一万个小时左右就一定能成为专家吗？遗憾的是，答案是否定的，因为我们大多数人都贪图舒适。

cues.en: For a lot of tasks in life, we can become competent in a fairly short period of time. Take driving a car for example. Initially, it's pretty challenging. It takes up all of system two, but after fifty hours or so, it becomes automatic. System one takes over and you can do it without much conscious thought. After that, more time spent driving doesn't improve performance. If you wanted to keep improving, you would have to try driving in challenging situations like new terrain, higher speeds, or in difficult weather. Now, I have played guitar for twenty five years, but I'm not an expert because I usually play the same songs. It's easier and more fun. But in order to learn, you have to be practicing at the edge of your ability, pushing beyond your comfort zone. You have to use a lot of concentration and methodically repeatedly attempt things you aren't good at. You can practice everything
cues.zh: 在生活中的许多任务上，我们都能在较短时间内达到熟练水平。以开车为例，刚开始时难度挺大，需要耗费全部的“系统二”，但在开了大约50小时后，操作就变得自动化了。“系统一”接管过来，你无需过多思考就能开好。自那之后，花再多时间开车也不会提高技术了。如果你想继续提升，就必须在更具挑战性的场景下尝试驾驶，比如陌生地形、更高车速或恶劣天气。就我而言，我弹了25年吉他，但我并不是大师，因为我总是在弹相同的曲子，这样更轻松也更有趣。但要想学有所得，你就必须在自己能力的边缘练习，逼自己走出舒适区。你必须高度专注，有条理地反复尝试自己不擅长的事。你可以把所有内容

cues.en: exactly as it is and exactly as it's written,
cues.zh: 丝毫不差地、完全按照原谱去练，

cues.en: but at just such a speed that you have to think about and and know exactly where you are and what your fingers are doing and what it feels like. This is known as deliberate practice. And in many areas, professionals don't engage in deliberate practice so their performance doesn't improve. In fact, sometimes it declines.
cues.zh: 但速度要压到这种程度：你必须边弹边想，明确知道自己弹到了哪一步、手指在做什么以及触感如何。这就是所谓的“刻意练习”。在许多领域，专业人士并不会进行刻意练习，所以他们的水平无法提升。事实上，有时甚至会退步。

cues.en: If you're experiencing chest pain and you walk into a hospital, would you rather the doctor is a recent graduate or or someone with twenty years experience?
cues.zh: 如果你感到胸痛走进医院，你更希望接诊的医生是刚毕业的新人，还是有二十年经验的老医生？

cues.en: Researchers have found that diagnostic skills of medical students increase with their time in medical school, which makes sense. The more cases you've seen with feedback, the better you are at spotting patterns. But this only works up to a point. When it comes to rare diseases of the heart or lungs, doctors with twenty years experience were actually worse at diagnosing them than recent graduates. And that's because they haven't thought about those rare diseases in a long time, so they're less able to recognize the symptoms.
cues.zh: 研究人员发现，医学生的诊断能力会随着医学院的学习年限而提高，这很合理。见过的有反馈的病例越多，识别规律的能力就越强。但这只在一定限度内有效。一旦涉及罕见的心肺疾病，拥有二十年经验的医生诊断准确率实际上比刚毕业的新人还要差。这是因为他们已经很久没接触过那些罕见病了，识别症状的能力自然就生疏了。

cues.en: Only after a refresher course could the doctors accurately diagnose these diseases.
cues.zh: 只有在参加进修课程之后，这些医生才能准确诊断出这些疾病。

cues.en: And you can see the same effect in chess. The best predictor of skill level is not the number of games or tournaments played, but the number of hours dedicated to serious solitary study.
cues.zh: 在国际象棋中你也能看到同样的现象。预测棋力水平的最佳指标，并不是对局或参赛的数量，而是投入到严肃独自钻研中的时间。

cues.en: Players spend thousands of hours alone learning chess theory, studying their own games and those of others. And they play through compositions,
cues.zh: 棋手们会花成千上万个小时独自学习棋理，研究自己和他人的棋谱。他们还会演练排局，

cues.en: which are puzzles designed to help you recognize tactical patterns.
cues.zh: 也就是专门用来帮你识别战术模式的残局谜题。

cues.en: In chess, as in other areas, it can be challenging to force yourself to practice deliberately.
cues.zh: 下国际象棋和其他领域一样，要强迫自己进行刻意练习往往很难。

cues.en: And this is why coaches and teachers are so valuable. They can recognize your weaknesses and assign tasks to address them.
cues.zh: 这也是教练和老师如此宝贵的原因。他们能看出你的弱点，并布置针对性的练习。

cues.en: To become an expert, you have to practice for thousands of hours in the uncomfortable zone attempting the things you can't do quite yet.
cues.zh: 要想成为专家，你必须在不适区练习数千小时，不断尝试那些你还做不好的事。

cues.en: True expertise is amazing to watch. To me, it looks like magic, but it isn't. At its core, expertise is recognition
cues.zh: 真正的专业表现令人叹为观止。在我看来它就像魔法，但其实不是。专业的核心在于识别能力，

cues.en: and recognition comes from the incredible amount of highly structured information stored in long term memory. To build that memory requires four things, a valid environment, many repetitions,
cues.zh: 而这种识别能力源于长期记忆中存储的海量高度结构化的信息。构建这种记忆需要四个要素：有效的环境、大量的重复、

cues.en: timely feedback, and thousands of hours of deliberate practice.
cues.zh: 及时的反馈，以及数千小时的刻意练习。

cues.en: When those criteria are met, human performance is astonishing.
cues.zh: 当满足这些条件时，人类的表现会惊人得强大。

cues.en: And when it's not, you get people we think of as experts who actually aren't.
cues.zh: 而如果不满足，就会出现那些我们以为是专家、但其实名不副实的人。

cues.en: If you want to become a STEM expert, you have to actively interact with problems.
cues.zh: 如果你想成为 STEM 领域的专家，就必须积极主动地去钻研问题。
